subtitle: Every family has this phone call: "Where do I click?" You are far away. You can't see their screen. They are scared to press the wrong thing. So I built Mate: a small light bulb on their Windows PC. They ask out loud. He shines a beam on the exact button. They click it themselves.

captions.text: Written by whoever set Mate up

subtitle: After each lesson, a card to keep. Muse Glimmer, Meta's open model on our own GPU, writes the steps. Muse Image draws the picture.

captions.text: Not on this screen, so he says so.

subtitle: And when he can't find it, he says so. He never guesses.

captions.text: What is going on on this page?

subtitle: He never presses Pay. Never Delete. Nothing with a password. If you ask, he presses a normal button, and only after you say yes. And passwords are painted black before anything leaves the PC.

This is how it really works. Muse Voice Transcribe hears you while you talk. Muse Spark finds the button in the list Windows gives us. MMS-TTS speaks. Every answer shows its model, its timing, and what was blacked out.
Seven Meta models. Each one has a job.

subtitle: You choose Mate's brain: quick, careful, or open weights on our own GPU.
We measured it. On forty made-up pages, he caught every scam.
When the button was on the screen and Windows listed it, he was right all six hundred ten times. Without that list, less than half. We report both numbers.
A son or daughter installs it once. A new app needs no new code where Windows lists its buttons. Where it doesn't, Mate says so.
One installer. No account to try. English and Russian today. Try it at meta-mate dot stream. Mate lights the button. Your parent clicks it.
